quest.title: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
quest.description: "The girl dreamed a very, very long dream. In it, people were holding hands, dancing in a circle, be they sages or fools, dancers or warriors, puppets or statues of gods... It did not matter who they were, or how old, and in that joyous dancing circle was the sum of all wisdom."
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1500, Mora x66000, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act X
chapter.title: Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution

talks.objective: Head to the entrance to King Deshret's mausoleum

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: I have not felt this way in a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Standing up high, gazing out at the rolling dunes... One cannot know what freedom truly means without first losing it.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: The Golden Slumber truly lives up to its name as a dreamland. Though desert sands exist there too, no mirage, no matter how glorious, can compare to true beauty.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Dendro Archon, what is on your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I was wondering... whose counsel I should seek on the questions in my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: What kind of questions?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So many... more than can be put into words.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As I once said to a friend: We look, we see, and we comprehend, but the question still troubles us.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: What are the many disasters that this world faces but the sum of all irresolvable questions?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: The biggest question you should be asking is how to seize victory.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, although I would express it differently:

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I must not fail. And so, the question I am most curious about now is whether the path to victory will be an arduous one.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: What we declare to be a young sapling we may, in fact, find to be a towering tree, if we would only cast aside our ignorance and look beyond the veil of time to see her true form.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Just in time. My preparations are almost complete.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ready when you are.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: We're here too!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Miss Nicole, Miss Nicole... you run so fast!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Phew... I thought I get a lot of exercise as a Forest Ranger, but I can barely keep up with you...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Sorry, I got a little carried away...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali, the equipment is ready, and the modifications to Aaru are all complete.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As discussed during our meeting...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Accessing Irminsul via the Akasha is no longer feasible at this stage. There are other options, it's just... They're a little more extreme, and more technologically demanding to implement.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Maybe you should take it from here.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The architecture and functionality of the Akasha Terminals overlap considerably with Aaru. There's reasonable evidence to suggest that one was developed based on the other, or that they both utilize technology of the same origin.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As long as the transplant and merge operation succeeds, Aaru should theoretically work on a scale greater than the Akasha, and approximately equal to Irminsul. It will become the largest active computing device in all of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: A system this powerful is capable of a lot of different things. In the past, the Akasha was primarily used for one-way information transmission, but I suspect it could also serve as a central bridging hub.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In the pursuit of greater knowledge, some scholars have attempted to connect their consciousness to Irminsul through the use of terminals, incense, and meditation.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Correct. In academic language, scholars who reach that stage are said to have entered Satyavada Life. Haypasia has performed this practice many times in the past, and she was once under my care for a period of time.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Right. And this at least proves that there is a zone within Irminsul that can be connected to.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's right. Providing wisdom to the people is one of the very reasons for Irminsul's existence. I think I understand where you're going. Please, continue.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In that case, I'll skip to the conclusion, then. We need to further modify Aaru, merge it with the Akasha, manufacture terminals, and distribute them to every single person we can reach.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Every person? Even the desert folk?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes. Everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I've already calculated the amount of raw materials we need.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So you mean, we're going to get new Akasha Terminals?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes — but this time, the people of Sumeru won't be using them to acquire knowledge, just to connect to Irminsul. That's the key.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: When we evacuated the city, we brought all the important assets from the House of Daena in case we ended up needing them. Fortunately, this included the Akasha System's main terminal.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We've checked all the relevant records, and one thing is certain: Nothing like this has ever been done on this scale before, so...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Everyone in Sumeru is part of the plan. Whoever controls the people controls the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Since this function of Irminsul was introduced, it has only ever been made available to scholars, who don't constitute a particularly large group of people.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But by expanding the scale to include all the people of Sumeru, all the individual connections will stack up to create a significant load on the system.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Under normal circumstances, Irminsul would be able to cope with the additional load. But with it already being under strain from other activities, its remaining capacity is limited.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Thus, it might be possible to shut it down completely by overloading it.

talks.objective: Head to the entrance to King Deshret's mausoleum

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This place looks so different from how I remember. It's unrecognizable.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a complete mess, like someone's turned the place upside down...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Must be Dottore's doing. Either he's searching for some information he needs, or...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's still changing.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He has to know we've entered Irminsul. But luckily for us, he can't pinpoint our location.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Be on your guard. Don't let him find us.

talks.objective: Head to the entrance to King Deshret's mausoleum

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Success! The evil Irminsul tree has stopped growing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Great!

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: What a display of true courage... the courage to think, and the courage to act. I never thought I would witness the shutdown of Irminsul with my own eyes... Perhaps this is human wisdom in action?

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Indeed, only humans could do such a thing. Gods are few and far between.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: What was once created for spreading knowledge is now used for another purpose... Heh, a rather ingenious plan.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I am grateful to you three for your help. Only thanks to you were we able to extend Aaru's interference capabilities to cover all terminals.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Now, nobody who wears a terminal will have their activity accurately tracked by Irminsul. No matter how many eyes Dottore possesses, he will not be able to see us clearly.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Now, for the next step...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I will need the help of your supreme powers once again.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: How might we be of service, Lord of Dendro?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I need to reach the Eternal Oasis immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right now!?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: In that case... Ibis King, would you agree that this is a fine opportunity to dust off our old tricks?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Nefer, I assume you have that chess set with you?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hehe, you mean the one you gave to me as a gift? Asking for it back, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: How could I? You misjudge me. I just wanted to show you another way you can use it.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Connect to Safhe Shatranj.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Safhe Shatranj? You mean that place in the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Thoth's chess set gains its power from the chessboard laid out in the desert by King Deshret and ourselves. All ceremonies conducted using the chess set must be activated via Safhe Shatranj.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: In other words, the chess set is an extension of the chessboard. In the past, moving a chess piece was a sacred and momentous act.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Transfer initiated... entering live combat mode.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Soldier
dialogues.text: We haven't heard a single word from our spy in the desert. I'm afraid he... might have been captured.
Never mind.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Soldier
dialogues.text: But we spent years turning him... And a lot of Mora...
Nothing comes for free in this world, but the loss is not without its purpose. For a small price, we have wasted a precious amount of the limited time they have. Quite a bargain, if you ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Soldier
dialogues.text: ...Understood.
Weighing profit against loss is a necessary part of life. But to tell the truth, I have been operating at a loss since this all began... since many centuries ago, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: For instance, why would a banker act as the executor of a will? If you hadn't deposited your personal belongings at Northland Bank, I would have no reason to be here right now.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Dottore, I've placed your final data backup into the Ley Lines as per our contract. I trust we are now square for the safe deposit fees you paid.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Is it not a little petty to split hairs like this, given our amicable relationship?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: I consider sound bookkeeping a matter of principle.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Do not forget that you only live to see this day thanks to me. In fact, every day of your life since you met me, you've been living on borrowed time.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Why, that's hardly a fair assessment. I will concede that my survival was perhaps at your whim, but I became a Harbinger on my own merits.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Managing money is not like other professions. Mine is not a role I could have acquired based on your recommendation alone, and certainly not one I could have lasted so long in without genuine ability.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: The information stored in the Ley Lines is quite comprehensive. Rest assured, I have not forgotten how strong your pride is.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Well? I presume you have no sense of fragmentation while talking with me.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: How could anything possibly go wrong with such strict measures in place? The remainder of your soul was split in two, with one half sent to Nod-Krai and the other stored in the most secure vault of the Northland Bank.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Though I must say, your disdain for the other Segments is quite amusing. Zandik is you, and you are Zandik. Zandik created the Segments — yet you, a Segment yourself, reject him.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: "I," that is, Zandik, created Segments of various ages in his later years. To achieve this, he had to freeze time and part with a portion of his soul.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: But as constructive as it sounds, it erases my uniqueness. If each Segment is equally me, then by the same token, none of them are truly me.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: A soul living forever in the past inevitably holds different views than he did in his later years. The same thing that completes me also restricts me.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: You too might ask yourself, which stage of your life you want to be preserved at? The day your business failed? Or the day you were framed by a gang and sold off to a medical lab as a test subject?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: ...We needn't dredge up the past.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: This undesirable plan was eventually scrapped. Lesser Lord Kusanali was quite right... I needed an opportunity to eliminate myself.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: And after that, I concluded that there was no more effective plan than directly splitting the soul. Once the soul is transferred out, you will find that creating a physical body is far simpler than creating a puppet.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: The other half of your soul suffered a crushing defeat in Nod-Krai, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: And yet in the process, I obtained the information I always wanted, did I not? Because now, we finally know where the best testing ground truly lies.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: I once thought your ultimate goal was to ascend to godhood. But as it turns out, that was merely one of your experiments.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Experiments take many forms. Most people are too eager for success, too fixated on the end goal. They forget that the experimental process itself is just as important.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: A suspiciously vacant seat, a new face... I trust you can put two and two together? The reason it doesn't exist is because someone tampered with the record.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: What can I say? After all your efforts, you really did uncover the world's secrets. So, is the "new world" you promised a lie?

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: No, it never was. I am glad to be able to control Irminsul from within... Now, I shall attempt to create a new world inside the existing one.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Almost everyone faces the prospect of death. But not a single person has ever been able to experiment unrestrained in the afterlife through sheer force of will.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: I am the only one to have overcome this enormous challenge. Would I not be letting the world down if I didn't make the most of the opportunity to experiment?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Clearly, the dividing of your soul did not affect the magnitude of your ego. Out of all the versions of you that have ever existed, this "you" is the most insane, and the most radical.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Is that why you chose to work with me? Which was it then... my insanity? Or my radicalism?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Could I call myself a venture capitalist without a suitably ambitious plan to invest in? Yours happened to fit the bill quite perfectly.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Well then, I must say... while I am surprised enough that you showed up at all, what surprises me more is that you chose to present yourself as my former subordinate and not as the banker, Pantalone.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Why make things harder than they need to be? Exposing my true identity in a situation like this would only serve to destroy diplomatic relations between Snezhnaya and Sumeru. I daren't imagine the consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Showing up in the name of the original antagonist gives you the recognition you rightly deserve, while also being sensitive to Snezhnaya's predicament. It was an easy win.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: As for why I'm here... If you're suggesting that your credit is in the negative, I won't argue with that. Many people say that about you.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: I'd argue that a significant factor in your willingness to cooperate is the fact that you have but a few years of life left after my death. Living and dying together has a way of binding two parties together rather closely.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Is it not true that a relationship should be judged by both the positive and negative returns it yields?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Haha, so some of what I said actually made it into your head after all. It's true that I hope you don't die too soon... but don't you find that a strange thing for me to say? After all, you've already had quite a long life.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: ...Especially for a human being.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Let's not pretend that you're any more innocent than I am. Are we not the same in this regard? We both despise the existing laws of this world, and neither of us enjoy being under anyone else's control.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Is it really so greedy to want the world to operate by a new set of rules?

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Of course not, my dear friend. And as I've said before, mutual interest is the foundation for the most reliable of relationships. You can attest to that.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Hehe. I just hope there never comes a day when I have to work too hard to prove that.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Soldier
dialogues.text: Regrator, Sir! People have been spotted approaching Sumeru City!

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: How strange... Despite your access to Irminsul's data, it appears the soldiers noticed before you did... They must have found a workaround.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Well, Dottore, I trust you know what this means? The fact is...

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: They're coming. They'll breach the city gates any moment now.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: But even so, I would say Irminsul is a wonderfully convenient thing on the whole. If you do manage to create a new world, perhaps you could plant one outside my office too?

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: I'll consider it.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: What do you need me to do? Stall them?

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: The experiment will take time. Stall them for as long as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Very well, but you're really asking for the moon here.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Have you heard this story? There was once a guilty man, kneeling in the center of a church, while an angry mob outside waited to bring him to justice.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: He pleaded with the gods, begging them to grant him one final request: the chance to finish confessing his sins before he was sentenced.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Many suns and moons passed, seasons changed, and still his confession continued, as if he intended to speak until the end of time...

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Are you suggesting I worship you as a god? Or were you hoping that I might confess my sins to you?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Certainly not the latter. That would make my life miserable indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: And speaking of gods...

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: For someone who despises them so, you never seemed to have any objections to me creating or becoming one.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: At first, I thought you'd be furious.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Concerned I would terminate our partnership, were you?

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Not at all. You had reasons why our partnership must continue.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Don't you find people's attitudes toward gods amusing? A god descends from the heavens, and people worship it unreservedly, blindly following whatever rules are given to them.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: And yet, when they see an ordinary person gain godlike levels of power by virtue of their own hard work, they treat him with nothing but suspicion, even if he is a compatriot.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Is that supposed to be a compliment?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: No. I was just thinking... I pity the man who would call you a compatriot.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: There's no need to be so self-critical.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The power of King Deshret's Seven Pillars is truly remarkable. With just a chessboard, you can move an entire unit across the material plane.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah, sets us up for a much easier fight. Really makes my day... The last time we stormed the city, it involved a lot more running around.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I wonder how many people can say they stormed a city twice in their lifetime...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I was just thinking that. I've definitely had more than my fair share of unusual experiences in my life...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: This is my first time here, actually. We never usually leave Gandharva Ville...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I hope this'll be my last time.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Does everyone have to chime in? Can't we just fight?

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: What an amusing comment, my dear lady. Yet humans often alleviate tension via small talk, do they not?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Why is Candace's shield talking!?

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: Because the image on her shield is one of me, and I, of course, can appear wherever I wish to.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Huh!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Well, lah-dee-dah, isn't that fancy. Could I get in on this?

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: You wish for your gauntlet to speak? Why, certainly.

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: Ahem. I think you'll find that it is I whose image is carved hereupon.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Thanks. Definitely feel stronger now.

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: You're welcome, my lady. I am glad to lend you my power.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cyno, what's the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There are troops stationed at every entrance. As we expected, a frontal assault will suffice.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Everyone, stick to the plan. We'll take the main entrance, you head for the House of Daena's side door.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Move out!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm trapped...!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Tsk, why won't this thing budge?
Hello? Helloooo...? Can you hear me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nicole? Is that you?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes, it's me. I'm monitoring your progress from inside the Eternal Oasis — and I have to say, this terminal is simply marvelous! It makes tracking you so much easier.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I couldn't see anything at first, but now that you two are inside, I can use your location with support from the terminals to get a partial view of the situation inside Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It's not the clearest image, but it's better than not being able to help at all. So, here I am!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I can't intervene directly, but I can help to guide you out of the jam you're currently in. So please, just follow my lead.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Waterway secured.

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Mercenary
dialogues.text: Brothers, sisters!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Perfect, just in time.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Welcome. Once we've linked up, we'll continue the advance.

dialogues.speaker: Corps of Thirty Soldier
dialogues.text: The team has arrived at the north entrance as planned.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Good. Press on.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Look out, it's an ambush!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Finally.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We need to hurry. Take the middle road, now!

dialogues.speaker: Corps of Thirty Soldier
dialogues.text: Mahamatra Cyno! Area clear!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Don't relax just yet. More Fatui approaching from the right!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Irminsul cannot track our movements. If necessary, we can split up.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Don't worry. We'll wipe them all out.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: As you can see, our people came raring to go.

dialogues.speaker: Corps of Thirty Soldier
dialogues.text: Good, good.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #How are things with {NICKNAME}? Can Tighnari keep {M#him}{F#her} safe?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't underestimate Tighnari just because he's a Forest Watcher. He can handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Alright, you know that's not what I meant...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hm.

talks.objective: Enter the Sanctuary of Surasthana by stealth

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Cyno and the reinforcements have drawn the Fatui's fire away. It's our turn.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: By using a Clusterleaf of Cultivation, we can pass through certain terrain silently.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Good luck with that. We'll just fly up there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh yeah... Paimon forgot she could fly...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ready!

talks.objective: Enter the Sanctuary of Surasthana by stealth

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Fatui soldiers up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Careful.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Prepare for battle.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Hey, there's people over there.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You have some nerve showing your faces here in the center of Sumeru City.
You're right on schedule.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Well, this guy sure as heck isn't your average Fatui Sergeant.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: (They've stationed quite a few people nearby. It definitely looks like they were waiting for us. But... something feels off.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: (Everything about this guy feels too deliberate. I highly doubt he's just a subordinate of Dottore's, and he's no mere sergeant... Whatever his rank is, it's high. Much higher than we thought.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So you've been waiting for us. But it looks like you're geared up for a conversation rather than a battle.
Very clever, General Mahamatra Cyno. I know you're the one in charge of this siege, and I look forward to making a deal with you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: A siege? Sumeru City belongs to us!
Historically, yes, but things can always change. We have quite a sizable force with us, you know. For instance...

dialogues.speaker: Runner, Corps of Thirty
dialogues.text: There's a Fatui ambush at the north gate!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Can you handle them?

dialogues.speaker: Runner, Corps of Thirty
dialogues.text: We can for now!
Yes, I'm quite sure both sides can hold their ground for the time being. The battle has not yet reached its climax.
But what happens next? Do you enjoy watching bloodshed? Surely, some of those here are people you count as friends?
Once a war begins, some people must die. I doubt you wish that fate upon anyone you know.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: (Wait a second... It's a trick! He's not even there!)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Silence!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: He disappeared! What was that? A—A ghost?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Curses... He was never there to begin with. That was just a shadow, projected there to lure us in.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Enough talk. Attack!
Haha, I apologize for being unable to accompany you at this crucial moment, but I am compelled to leave for reasons beyond my control. Please excuse me.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Sumeru's General Mahamatra is quite ruthless. It's a good thing I wasn't there in person.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Your illusion held them up for a time just fine. But now that they have seen through it, they will realize you were just a decoy.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Decoy or not, what matters now is that they will be heading your way imminently.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Not imminently. They are already here.

talks.objective: Enter the Sanctuary of Surasthana by stealth

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We made it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is far enough. Tighnari, you go help Cyno. Don't worry about us — we'll manage from here.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Are you sure you don't need me to stand guard?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No need. Once the connection is established, we'll disappear from the Sanctuary of Surasthana. Go help the others.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright... Goodbye for now, then. Please tread carefully.

talks.objective: Enter the Sanctuary of Surasthana by stealth

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: We can connect to the inside of Irminsul through the Sanctuary of Surasthana's built-in security system.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You should be pretty familiar with the process.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it the same route as last time?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: For the most part. We don't need to adjust any of the parameters.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then I should be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: And Paimon? Once you're both ready, we'll set off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, the stakes are way higher this time, right? Maybe Paimon should stay outside and help the others. Then you can focus on the fight without having to worry about Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? ...Why are you staring at me like that?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...It's nothing. I just suddenly realized how much you've grown.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey, you've grown quite a lot yourself. Don't you two start getting into it again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, well anyway, Paimon thinks she's pretty knowledgeable. Who's the best guide in Teyvat, again? And don't forget, Paimon's a college student now!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If we say Alhaitham's not a weirdo, it's hard to explain how he came up with the idea of you applying to the Akademiya... But for all that he counts, you're doing surprisingly well in your studies.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just goes to show how important it is to have someone supporting you! And Paimon's not the only one — let's not forget that you only became a student because of Nahida's personal recommendation.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: That's fair. I have learned a lot in Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Oh yeah... Did you ever come up with that ugly nickname you promised me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? No way, we're friends now! Paimon gave up on giving you one ages ago! ...Anyway, isn't "Hat Guy" enough of a nickname for you?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hah... Fine, suit yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We need to go. Paimon, if you're staying... look after yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will do. Paimon's gonna link up with Tighnari and Cyno. You guys are the ones who need to be careful!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We will be. Bye for now.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Initiating connection!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Well, here we are again.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, I still don't even know where we're going.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks to our terminals, it should be impossible for Irminsul to read. I can—

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Don't. Don't tell me. Only you need to know. That way, whatever happens to me next, it won't affect your progress.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Listen to me. Your safety is just as important as mine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't even think about sacrificing yourself for the greater good. We came here together, and we're leaving together.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Alright, if you insist. I won't argue with you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Phew! I think we've made it to relative safety...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You doing okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll be fine, don't worry.
Look at you, supporting one another. How very touching.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dottore!?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hmph. Took you long enough to find us. You're more useless than I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Oh, really? I think I deserve a little more credit for my methods than that.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Rather than hunting you down, I chose to let you roam free...

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: I indulged your presumption that I was unable to track your movements, played along with your clever little plan...

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Fleeing is for animals, but I rather enjoy watching you flee. Some things lose the will to run altogether as soon as you put them in a cage.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If that's true, then why did you come looking for us?

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Because I wanted to observe you up close, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Don't misunderstand me, I'm not here for a fight. Is it so unusual that I wished to greet my old acquaintances in person?

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: After all... It's been a while, Scaramouche.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He remembers!? No, that can't be it, it's impossible...)

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Why are you so afraid? I have done nothing unprecedented in discovering the truth, nor did I go to any great lengths to uncover your story.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: You made a bold series of moves in deciding to erase yourself, and with the power of this great chronicling device called Irminsul, you were able to achieve something quite remarkable.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Once most people form an opinion about someone, it tends to imprison their mind. Yet you managed to erase every trace of your existence. A novel take on death indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: However, this meant that you stood out to me all the more when I saw you in Nod-Krai. I didn't even have to go looking for you — just the sight of you was enough for me to intuit the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: For someone in my position, connecting the dots was a trivial affair. It would have been more surprising if I hadn't managed to piece it together.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hmph... You seem very pleased with yourself for figuring it out. I'm sure you'd even be more delighted to learn the full extent of your crimes.

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: That would hardly be necessary. Besides, isn't there something that concerns you more right now? Something that fills you with dread?

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: Let me put your mind at ease: I have no intention whatsoever of restoring any of the records you deleted. For one thing, it would be exceptionally difficult. But more to the point...

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: I doubt that the prospect of losing your current life is all that frightening to you. Because in your case... Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Il Dottore
dialogues.text: The cruelest twist of fate is that you'll never again have the chance to make up for any of your mistakes, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Dottore!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Whew! Goodness, that was tough.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Take a short rest, and then—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nicole? Nicole!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: The connection's been cut? But that means...

talks.objective: Defeat your opponents with everything that you've got
Proclaim the inevitability of the action
Proclaim the inevitability of the action
Proclaim the inevitability of the action

dialogues.speaker: Ruler of Death
dialogues.text: Blessed One of Wisdom, Mahakusaladhamma, are you certain that you wish to exercise your authority to destroy Irminsul?

dialogues.speaker: Ruler of Death
dialogues.text: It represents both your roots and your finest accomplishments. You truly intend to abandon the very thing you have always fought for?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This is my decision. Irminsul has been corrupted beyond redemption.

dialogues.speaker: Ruler of Time
dialogues.text: Irminsul is the original tree of Teyvat. It is the means by which the Heavenly Principles maintains fate itself. The Seven Archons should honor and revere it, for their authority was bestowed upon them by the Heavenly Principles.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It is precisely because I honor and revere it that I fight for the humanity it exists to protect.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Wisdom is knowing how to weigh the options and make the right decision. If you truly care about the fortunes of this world, then it is me you should seek to preserve.

dialogues.speaker: Ruler of Life
dialogues.text: Mhmhm...

dialogues.speaker: Ruler of Life
dialogues.text: Planting a seed begins the chain of cause and effect. Since you have become a great tree yourself, why should the loss of another tree be anything to fear?

dialogues.speaker: Ruler of Life
dialogues.text: Till we meet again, Lord of Dendro.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: ...What a magnificent fire.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: In Snezhnaya, we light fires to ward off the cold. Fire, it seems, is antithetical to ideas such as cold, frozen, and unchanging.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Perhaps it has always been that way. From the beginning, fire has been used to drive away wild beasts and warm the body and mind... You could say it's a form of treatment. One that cures the human heart of mortal fear.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Mortal fear... Haha, something you haven't been acquainted with in a long time, by the sounds of it.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Whereas you, I'm sure, must know the feeling quite well indeed. I remember when we first discussed the elixir of immortality, you claimed that extending your lifespan was about buying more time. But was that really the truth?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You fear the prospect of dying a wretched end in this world, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Of course I do. I'm only human, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: And while you may have forgotten it, you cannot deny that you, too, were once human, Dottore. I do not believe that there is no such fear in your heart.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Perhaps you're right. But I abandoned it long ago and devoted myself to my experiments. I have felt no fear since.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: From the very beginning, I never thought you could win this game.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: But still you came, contract in hand, to honor our agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Because I am a reputable partner.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: And, as we have discussed, experiments are about more than results alone — the process is equally important. I have come here and completed my creation... and I do not regret my decision.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: I'm afraid your journey ends here.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: After I die, there will be no one to make the elixir of immortality, and your remaining stock will only last a few more years. How then will you prove that you didn't perish in this incident alongside everyone else?

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: When I feel optimistic about market environments, I never forcibly adjust them — they have their own direction. And I myself am one such environment.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: I have been quite particular about many things in my life. But where the manner of my death is concerned, I choose not to be.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You make yourself sound so magnanimous.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: Oh, but I am, and I hope you will be too. It may have been a long time since anyone told you this, Dottore, but I recognize that you are a truly rare talent.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: ...Hah.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I can see it... The experiment in blasphemy that I've been performing all this time...

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: It has been a long process. And I do not care about the results as much as people might imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: If the very goal of your experiment was to explore infinite possibilities, then there was never any reason for it to end.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Indeed. Yet now... the experiment has officially drawn to a close.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: What should I call you? Zandik? Or do you prefer Dottore?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Suit yourself. Goodbye, Feofan. This time, that's what it truly is.

dialogues.speaker: Regrator
dialogues.text: And don't I know it. Goodbye, Zandik.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I could have carried out many more experiments... but to me, Lord of Dendro, this outcome is certainly not the worst.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I believe you. But unfortunately, this is where it all ends for you. This experiment does not belong to you, nor do any of the results.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: "Experiment"... It sounds like you're trying to outdo me in my own field.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Wisdom is conveying information in terms that people can clearly understand. You know exactly what I mean.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: ...Indeed, I can see no further outcomes.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Hah... You have a formidable mind, and you are braver than I thought. Setting fire to the very thing your survival depends on... Your previous threat was empty, but this time, it is real.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: When necessary, wisdom can be as fierce as an inferno. Some of the flames that incinerate you come from within yourself.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Perhaps you are right. You see what lies at the bottom of the human heart, and that is your wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Here is where your journey comes to an end. All that is yet unknown belongs to those of us who will carry on living.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: ...It seems I have unwittingly been your arch-enemy all along. But now, it's all over.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I do not deny your intelligence. But what you refer to as "experiments" I would never describe in those terms.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: They are events that take place in the real world, and they are so much more than mere data.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Goodbye. We will never meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Time to go! Let's meet the others at the Mausoleum of King Deshret!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Out of my way!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Take this!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Aah!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Get lost!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Whew... Thank you, Jeht...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You gotta be more careful. If you're not ready to put your life on the line, you can't be certain of defeating your opponent.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, she's right. Keep your wits about you, Rana.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Take them out and secure the harbor! Reinforcements will arrive by water.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Consider it done.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Show no mercy!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This isn't the route we planned. We can't afford to stray.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Don't hang your head so low. We don't want you falling down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, now where's the interface Nahida mentioned? C'mon, where's it hiding...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Found it. It's over here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's time!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Say your prayers!
